RequestedObject.Name: Vulnerability Library
RequestedObject.Description:
The Vulnerability Library application represents a catalog of vulnerability data collected from the National Vulnerabilities Database (NVD)/National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), QualysGuard, and Tenable Security Center. The Vulnerability Library is updated each week or month by data feeds depending on the source. The library includes data points such as:
• Vulnerability publication date
• Title
• Consequence
• Recommended solution
• Severity
• CVSS scoring 


Records can be linked to affected devices, vulnerability scan results, and malicious code found to exploit the vulnerability.  The vulnerability library also provides a method for generating exception requests, identifying mitigating strategies, and denoting affected ports.

By tying vulnerabilities to assets you can properly analyze, prioritize, and respond proactively to address the threat for vulnerable assets. The Vulnerability Library provides the ability to:
• Automatically import data from NVD/NIST, QualysGuard, and Security Center.
• Notify appropriate personnel automatically when new vulnerabilities are identified.
• Research potential threats and produce real-time reports that aid in the creation of action plans.

RequestedObject.Name: Business Impact Analysis
RequestedObject.Description:
The Business Impact Analysis (BIA) enables organizations to inventory their customer-facing products or services and dependencies (internal business processes, systems, people, locations, etc.) used to produce them. The BIA is an analysis tool designed to apply decision criteria to help organizations determine the criticality and impact tolerances (monetary and non-monetary) for each product or service. The BIA may also be used to determine criticality at the business process level per traditional business continuity approaches. A BIA should be completed for each product and service, or for each business process, depending on the methodology used by the organization.

Resulting criticality ratings and impact tolerances provide focus to then be used prioritize efforts to build resilience into producing and providing the products or services across the related dependencies.

RequestedObject.Name: Loss Events

The Loss Events application allows you to record actual and near miss losses that impact your organization or other organizations, whether they originate from internal or external events. You can document and manage loss events, loss categories, detection source, control factors, root cause analysis, insurance and claims activities, and remediation activities. Additionally, you can relate loss events to business processes and risk register items and account for them as metrics that influence residual risk calculations.

Through the Loss Events application, you can:
•Centralize the documentation of losses, categorize them for reporting purposes, and track projected and actual loss amounts.
•Utilize configurable work flow to auto-notify staff of their responsibilities for documenting, analyzing and responding to losses.
•Perform root cause analyses to determine the likelihood of event reoccurrence and to identify failed controls, violated policies and related losses.
•Relate loss events to the Risk Register to quantify the likelihood and impact of risks based on loss data.
•Integrate general ledger information from your existing systems using the Data Feed Manager to automate the tracking of financial losses, offsets and recovery.
•Track recovery tasks and activities.
•Evaluate losses against existing insurance policies and manage claims handling

RequestedObject.Name: Risk Hierarchy
RequestedObject.Description:
This Risk Hierarchy application coupled with the Risk Register application creates a 3 level risk roll-up solution. This application enables an organization to roll-up their risks from the risk register to an intermediate summary level, and then to an enterprise summary level. This application stores a company's risk hierarchy in the form of two levels - Enterprise Summary Level and Intermediate Summary Level. Enterprise Risks (the top level) are risks that are described very broadly at the highest level of an organization; they represent an accumulation of all of the intermediate summary risks. Intermediate summary risks are summary level risks that lie between the Risk Register and Enterprise Risk. Intermediate summary risks are then associated with Risk Register records to track risks via Metrics, Control Compliance, and Risk Assessments.

They are regularly updated during the audit process and include requested supporting documents that auditors need from clients, such as policies, reports, and so on. Auditors use the PBC lists to begin fieldwork tests and understand the controls and processes within scope. Auditors can add new requests to the PBC list as needed for the audit.

 

Use Case Version: Financial Controls Monitoring 6.8

Use Case Version: Audit Engagements & Workpapers 6.10
Use Case Version: Audit Planning 6.10

RequestedObject.Name: Process Narratives
RequestedObject.Description:
Process Narratives document major financial flows and processes. The Process Narratives application manages these records while Narrative step records provide more granular detail. These narratives are documented and reviewed for SOX Act 302 certification. They are also subject to a Change Control process to ensure that changes are reviewed and approved prior to being implemented.

 

Use Case Version: Financial Controls Monitoring 6.8
Use Case Version: Audit Engagements & Workpapers 6.10
Use Case Version: Audit Planning 6.10

RequestedObject.Name: Audit Observations
RequestedObject.Description:
The Audit Observations application is used to document deficiencies or gaps found through the audit workpaper control testing. Through the Audit Observations application, you can:
Review Observations that are captured through the results of workpaper control testing.
Capture/identify  appropriate personnel, and track tasks associated with Audit Observations resolution.
Mitigate Audit Observations through remediation tasks or exception requests.

Use Case: Audit Engagements & Workpapers 6.10

RequestedObject.Name: Operational Scenario Library
RequestedObject.Description:
The Operational Scenario Library application serves as a catalog of Operational Scenario templates. Those templates can be used to generate new Operational Scenario Analysis records without having to create them from scratch. Those scenarios can then be used to test impact tolerances against the defined scenario types.

Use Case Version: Operational Scenario Analysis 6.11

RequestedObject.Name: Scenario Results
RequestedObject.Description:
The Scenario Results application leverages the Scenario Results Creation Feed to merge portions of Impact Tolerance and Scenario Analysis Results records to be used for testing. A record is created for each impact tolerance being tested as part of a scenario. The actual period of disruption, and quantitative and qualitative results for each scenario can be input which are then compared against the predefined impact tolerance. Any metric that exceeds the predefined tolerance will result in a failed impact tolerance record. Additionally, users can identify the failed resource among the dependency chain. Scenario Results that fall outside of impact tolerances automatically generate findings and the formal issues management process can be followed.

Use Case Version: Operational Scenario Analysis 6.11

RequestedObject.Name: Operational Scenario Analysis
RequestedObject.Description:
The Operational Scenario Analysis application enables organizations to test predefined impact tolerances against severe, yet plausible scenarios such as cyber events, pandemics, natural disasters, supply chain disruptions, or data breaches. Scenarios can be linked to key organizational pillars, such as cyber resilience, IT resilience, facilities, people, or third parties. Multiple impact tolerances can be tested for each scenario, and then the results are rolled up to the parent scenario. For failed impact tolerances, the point of failure among the supporting assets can be identified for reporting purposes.

Use Case Version: Operational Scenario Analysis 6.11

RequestedObject.Name: Resilience Threat Register
RequestedObject.Description:
The Resilience Threat Register is used to document known threats and associate them to specific Operational Scenarios or BC/DR plans. As threats are identified through various sources, for example enterprise risk management efforts, or trends, those applicable to a target of BC planning should be included in the Resilience Threat Register.

Use Case Version: BC/DR Planning 6.10

Use Case Version: Operational Scenario Analysis 6.10

RequestedObject.Name: Impact Tolerances
RequestedObject.Description:
The Impact Tolerances application enables organizations to define the maximum tolerable period of disruption to important products and services as well to identify the type of impact such as impact to customers, partners, third parties, financial institutions, and more.  Impact tolerances should always be expressed as a unit of time - hours, days, or weeks, but can also include other metrics such as financial loss, impact to reputation, regulatory impact, and consumer impact. Impact tolerances can also be defined over time to identify the resilience during each time period.

Use Case Version: Operational Scenario Analysis 6.10

RequestedObject.Name: Third Party Campaign
RequestedObject.Description:
The Third Party Campaign application is used to bulk create Zero-Day Vulnerability or Location Based Risk assessments. The application allows users to document high level information about recent software vulnerabilities or geographical risk events, and choose which Third Parties will be the target of the assessment. A data feed will then generate assessments for each Third Party selected in the record.

Use Case Version: Third Party Governance 6.12

RequestedObject.Name: Service Interruptions
RequestedObject.Description:
The Service Interruptions application is used to detail and compare the impact of incidents against predefined impact tolerances. After documenting the details of an incident, users can select the products and services affected and the corresponding impact tolerances to test. A data feed copies details of the incident and impact tolerance into the Service Interruption Results application where the actual period of disruption and impact tolerance are compared. Incidents that exceed the time threshold set in the Impact Tolerance record will prompt the user to document lessons learned. Although users can link records from the Incidents and Loss Events application to the service interruption,  those applications are not prerequisites.

Use Case Version: Operational Scenario Analysis 6.12

RequestedObject.Name: Service Interruption Results
RequestedObject.Description:
The Service Interruption Results application uses the Service Interruption Results Creation data feed to merge portions of Service Interruption and Impact Tolerance records for testing. A record is created for each impact tolerance being tested as part of the Service Interruption. After creation, the actual period of disruption from the Service Interruption and maximum tolerable period of disruption from the Impact Tolerance are compared. If the maximum tolerable period of disruption is exceeded, then the user is prompted to complete a Lessons Learned section and document why the impact tolerance was exceeded.

Use Case Version: Operational Scenario Analysis 6.12

RequestedObject.Name: Resilience Scorecard
RequestedObject.Description:
The Resilience Scorecard application automatically scores the resilience of each business unit, division, and company across the 5 resilience pillars - cyber, facilities, IT, people, and suppliers. Resilience ratings are calculated by equally weighting results of Operational Scenario Analysis, Operational Resilience Assessments, Metrics, Third Party Metrics, and Third Party Resilience Assessments linked to the resilience pillar and the business unit, or business units in the division or the company. Ratings are only calculated for business units, divisions, and the company if they have data points tied to that resilience pillar. The ratings are automatically created by the Generate Resilience Scorecard Records data feed.

Use Case Version: Operational Scenario Analysis 6.12
